items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: I tried to take Edmund Hall, plays with Buddy Petit when Edmund Hall left.

ctx.x: Did you hear Edmund Hall over there?
Yes. I tried to take Edmund Hall, plays with Buddy Petit when Edmund Hall left.
Did he play the same as he plays now? Almost. Almost. Would Zeb have a tone like him or more like yours? Zeb had a tone more like Edmund Hall. What about Georgie Boyd? What kind of tone did he have?

items.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan…
items.q: me, Edmund Hall, Robert Hall, we all organized a little band

ctx.x: How did you get a job with it?

Oh, we used to get a lot of work. People, them days, them days wasn't like people today, you know? Anything you do, if you take a tin pan and hit on that dance, you see? But them days, you know what I mean, that's how it was, you see? So, well, we, after that, when we began, me, Edmund Hall, Robert Hall, we all organized a little band, you see? We got a band together, then we began to play, you know, out in the country where I'm from, reserve, you see? So we played for this fella, putting here three or four…
And you did name it that then?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: Edmund Hall got in the Buddy Petit's band, and I stayed with Leonard Parker... So when uh, Edmund Hall left him

ctx.x: But did you live there all the time or just for the summers?

No, you see, my family and I, we were minding a club, and regalese, and I was a club, and regalese, you know? And uh, my oldest daughter, Mildred, she was a small child, she was taken with terrible fever from mosquito bites, and the doctor ordered me to take her, thought probably she had some lung trouble or something, to bring her over there in his party. But my father was over in that neighborhood, so I just brought her. Well I joined the Black Eagles band, and I played with Leonard Parker, and uh, uh, Fritz…
When you came back over here, you worked with Billy and the Dee some, didn't you?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: I came over here after the band is all where Edmund Hall left the band... when, uh, uh, Hall left that band. They used to play the Jackson Square in Manorville.

ctx.x: What about this guy, who's called Fritz?

Fritz had a good term, but not compared to none of the people. He was a... Fritz had a term, something like... I used to say something like Edmund Hall or something. Sure. That's sort of a tone yet. But, uh, it was very fast. And you knew what he was doing. But for a tone, you can have a tone like it. You take Edmund Hall or a tone like it, but it was more... Raw than some new musicians that you would get. Although I'm not knocking them easy at first class musicians. Stone was not the same with me.
Yeah. What about Fritz's ideas? Well, I think... Man, I think it was Chris...
